Q0002 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
A large piece of wood is right in front of you while driving on a suburban street and there is no other option than to driver over it. What should you do to keep control? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Jump off the bike
  • [B] Rise slightly in your seat ✔ Correct
  • [C] Straighten up the bike ✔ Correct
  • [D] Loosely hold the grips to absorb any shock
Explanation: You should hold onto the hand grips firmly and straighten up the bike, rise slightly in your seat, and keep a neutral balance.
Q0003 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
A learner motorcyclist is on an open road, what is the maximum speed?
  • [A] 50kph
  • [B] 60kph
  • [C] 80kph
  • [D] 100kph ✔ Correct
Explanation: Since Oct. 1 2011, a learner motorcyclist can drive on open road at a maximum of 100kph.
Q0004 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers

  • [A] Drivers of other vehicles fail to look
  • [B] Motorcyclists wear dark colours and are hard to see
  • [C] Compared to a car a motorcycle has a small profile ✔ Correct
  • [D] Saccades - minute eye movements that render us blind for fractions of a second at a time ✔ Correct

  • [E] Boots

Q0006 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
An engine seizure is caused by:
  • [A] Changing up a gear too early
  • [B] Not changing gear properly
  • [C] Not enough lubrication in the engine ✔ Correct
  • [D] Damp weather
Explanation: A lack of lubrication causes engine seizure because without oil, the engine's moving parts can't move smoothly against one another. This causes the engine to overheat.
Q0007 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you permitted to pass like this on the left?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: You are permitted to pass on the left if there are two lanes on your side of the road and it's safe to do so.
Q0008 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Are you permitted to pass on a solid yellow line?
  • [A] No
  • [B] Yes
  • [C] If you can make the pass without crossing the yellow line and can see 100m in front of you for the whole time you are passing then you can pass ✔ Correct
Explanation: As long as you stay to the left of the yellow line in this situation then you can pass a car.

  • [C] Brake before the curve ✔ Correct

Q0011 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Can you stop or park your vehicle anytime at a broken yellow line painted close to the edge of the road? True or False?
  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct
Explanation: You can't park your vehicle on a broken yellow line.

  • [C] It keeps the face of the rider warm in cooler temperatures
  • [D] It's impossible to breath without one above 80kph

Q0014 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Counter steering best enables you to do what?
  • [A] Maintain a straight line
  • [B] Swerve around an object ✔ Correct
  • [C] Controls the bike around corners
Explanation: Counter steering is a way of turning quickly on a motorcycle.

Q0016 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Engine seizure is usually imminient when:
  • [A] Loss of power and a change in the sound ✔ Correct
  • [B] More power
  • [C] Shrieks and pops coming from the exhaust
  • [D] Blue and red smoke emerging from the unit
Explanation: Correct. The power drops and there may be a change in the engine tone, as well when an engine is about to seize.
Q0017 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Holding your knees against the petrol tank will help you do what the most?
  • [A] Build strength to help with control
  • [B] Go faster
  • [C] Better mileage
  • [D] Balance ✔ Correct
Explanation: The main benefit of holding your knees is that it will help you to balance and may make you more aerodynamic.
Q0018 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How much braking is generated from using the front wheel?
  • [A] 0.5
  • [B] 0.6
  • [C] 0.7
  • [D] More than 70% ✔ Correct
Explanation: 75-90% of the braking performance comes from the front brake.
Q0019 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
How often does your motorcycle require a Warrant of Fitness inspection if your motorcycle was first registered before the 1st of January 2000?
  • [A] 12 months
  • [B] 6 months ✔ Correct
  • [C] 2 years
  • [D] 1.5 years
Explanation: You will need to take it for a WoF every six months if your bike was first registered before 1 January 2000.

Q0024 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers

Q0026 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Motorbike - Motorbike-Specific DT Driver Training (Extended)
If you hold your knees against the petrol tank as you ride, what will it do?
  • [A] Stop you from getting cold
  • [B] Go faster
  • [C] Improve fuel economy
  • [D] Balance as the motorbike turns ✔ Correct

Q0027 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Road-position Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
If you intend to move your vehicle from the right-hand lane to the left-hand lane, what must you do? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Indicate left for three seconds ✔ Correct
  • [B] Check your blind spot over your left shoulder ✔ Correct
  • [C] Look in your rear view mirror ✔ Correct
Explanation: All three of these things you should do.

Q0029 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If you need to slow in a curve, how should you do it?
  • [A] Use both brakes gently ✔ Correct
  • [B] Only use the front brake gently
  • [C] Only use the rear brake gently
Explanation: Correct. Always brake on the straight before it's too late, brake gently and try to avoid having to slow in a curve all together. Note that in this situation some motorcycle instructors advise you to only use the rear brake, which contradicts NZTA's information on this question.
Q0030 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA & DT Driver Training

  • [A] The engine dies and you lose power
  • [B] Engine over-revs and you lose power ✔ Correct
Explanation: Mechanical failure in motorbikes The types of mechanical failure that would give the largest cause for concern when riding your bike are engine seizure, brake failure, tyre failure and your chain breaking. If your chain breaks the engine will rev higher and you will lose power....
Q0031 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
If your vehicle breaks down on a motorway, what should you do? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Get out on the motorway and flag someone down to stop and help
  • [B] Open your boot and bonnet ✔ Correct
  • [C] Turn your hazard lights on ✔ Correct
  • [D] Call for assistance using your cell phone or a motorway phone. ✔ Correct
  • [E] Park as far to the left as possible ✔ Correct
Explanation: You should hang something white on your car door handle and open your boot and bonnet to indicate you need help. Put on your hazard lights, keep away from the motorway and call for help.
Q0032 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
If your vehicle is not up to warrant of fitness standard, can you be fined if it is on the road?
  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No
Explanation: Correct. If something appears to not be up to warrant of fitness standard then a police office can inspect your call by pulling you over.
Q0033 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a line of stopped or moving traffic, what should you do?
  • [A] Drive on the right past the traffic
  • [B] Drive on the left past the traffic
  • [C] Stay in the centre of your lane ✔ Correct
  • [D] Stay in the right hand side of your lane
  • [E] Stay in the left hand side of your lane
Explanation: Be as visible as possible by staying in the middle of your lane and protect your lane position from other vehicles. Avoid squeezing by other traffic to reduce your risk of an accident.
Q0034 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In a situation when you are passing parked vehicles, the main dangers include: vehicles pulling out without signalling or vehicles making U-turns when you are passing parked vehicles. True or false?
  • [A] TRUE ✔ Correct
  • [B] FALSE
Explanation: Yes. A motorcyclist has an advantage over drivers when passing parked vehicles because, by staying in the right-hand lane one can avoid problems like drivers getting out of other vehicles, doors opening or people stepping out from between vehicles.
Q0035 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
In addition to checking to see if it is safe to move out from the kerb into the traffic flow, how long should you indicate for?
  • [A] 1 second
  • [B] 2 seconds
  • [C] 3 seconds ✔ Correct
  • [D] 5 seconds
Explanation: A safe time to signal for is three seconds.

  • [A] TRUE
  • [B] FALSE ✔ Correct

Q0037 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA & DT Driver Training

  • [A] Front ✔ Correct
  • [B] Middle
  • [C] Back
  • [D] On the opposite side of the road

Q0038 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Motorcyclists can suffer from Hypothermia. What could cause this?
  • [A] Not enough clothing
  • [B] Dehydration
  • [C] Lack of food
  • [D] Wind ✔ Correct
Explanation: Your core body temperatures drop dangerously low with Hypothermia, reducing your reflexes. It can be deceptive as even on a nice day hypothermia can occur due to the wind chill.

On a sealed road at a Give Way sign, what is the colour of the painted line?
  • [A] Yellow
  • [B] Blue
  • [C] White ✔ Correct
Explanation: The line is white.

Q0042 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Permitted you can do so safely, you may pass on the left at an intersection if:
  • [A] the vehicle beside you is going faster than the speed limit
  • [B] the vehicle behind is signalling a left turn
  • [C] you have your parking lights off
  • [D] the vehicle in front is signalling a right turn ✔ Correct
Explanation: You can pass left at an intersection if you are in another lane or in a turning bay or if a vehicle is indicating right and has moved over toward the right of their lane, then you can overtake on the left if it's safe to proceed and your vehicle will fit through the gap.
Q0043 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Intersection Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
Should you stop when coming up to a stop sign, and if so, where should you stop?
  • [A] Behind the marked line
  • [B] Where you can see traffic coming in both directions ✔ Correct
  • [C] If you can see that nothing is coming then you don't need to stop
  • [D] On the yellow line with the front wheels of your vehicle
Explanation: Yes, you must stop at a stop sign and you must stop in such a way that you can see if other traffic is coming.
Q0044 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The closest distance that your vehicle may be parked to a vehicle entrance is:
  • [A] One metre ✔ Correct
  • [B] Two metres
  • [C] Four metres
  • [D] Five metres
Explanation: Your vehicle can be parked 1 metre away, this gives vehicles space to turn out of and in to the entrance.
Q0045 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
The main reason for wearing protective clothing is what?
  • [A] Makes for a smoother ride
  • [B] To help prevent serious injury or death ✔ Correct
  • [C] To help other drivers see you better
Explanation: In an accident, protective clothing can increase your chance of survival.

Q0048 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Theory Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
What does a Warrant of Fitness show? Select all that apply.
  • [A] The vehicle is safe to be on the road
  • [B] An approved WoF inspector has inspected the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [C] The month the WoF expires ✔ Correct
Explanation: It's the driver's responsibility to ensure that the vehicle they are driving is safe and roadworthy at all times. The WoF label shows the month it was expected and the expiry and proves that the vehicle was roadworthy at time of inspection.

Q0050 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Signs Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0054 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Signs Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] Oncoming light rail

  • [C] Light rail crossing ahead ✔ Correct

Q0056 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] The left side of a bridge
  • [B] The right side of a bridge ✔ Correct

  • [D] Right hand side of the road
Explanation: The right side of the bridge is indicated by the marker.
Q0057 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Signs Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] A route for pedestrians only ✔ Correct
  • [B] School ahead
  • [C] No pedestrians permitted
  • [D] A route for cyclists only
Explanation: Correct. This sign states that no motor vehicles are allowed, as it marks a pedestrian zone.
Q0058 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Signs Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] Vehicles are merging off of a roundabout
  • [B] The left lane is closed ✔ Correct
  • [C] There's a fire hydrant ahead on the left
Explanation: This sign is usually erected by road workers and is a temporary warning.
Q0059 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Signs Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] Pedestrians only on this route
  • [B] Cyclists only on this route
  • [C] A route for pedestrians and cyclists ✔ Correct
  • [D] No pedestrians or cyclists permitted on this route
  • [E] No bicycle tricks permitted
Explanation: This sign indicates that pedestrians and cyclists share this route.

Q0066 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What is it best to do before going through a right hand curve?
  • [A] Move to the left hand side of the road
  • [B] Move to the right hand side of the road
  • [C] Slow down ✔ Correct
Explanation: Slowing down is the best plan, as new motorcycle riders often enter turns too quickly. They tend to cross into another lane of traffic or go off the road because they can't hold the turn, or they brake too hard and skid out of control.
Q0067 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

  • [A] 400mcg/litre of breath
  • [B] 350mcg/litre of breath
  • [C] 250mcg/litre of breath ✔ Correct
  • [D] 100mcg/litre of breath
  • [E] Zero
Explanation: Correct. The maximum permissible level is 250mcg/litre of breath, although any amount of alcohol affects your reaction times, so it is recommended you don't drink at all before driving.

Q0075 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi

Q0086 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Bike-specific Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers

  • [C] If the front wheel goes flat shift your weight as far back as possible ✔ Correct
  • [D] If the back tyre goes flat just sit normally ✔ Correct
Explanation: If possible, avoid braking and close the throttle gradually, letting the bike slowly stop. Signal and move to the side of the road and if your back tyre deflates keep your weight neutral. If your front tyre deflates move your weight to the back.

Q0090 Class 6 (Motorcycle) Core Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do in order to prevent being blinded by the headlights of oncoming traffic?
  • [A] Let the other driver know by flashing your lights
  • [B] Keep your eyes to the left of the road and slow down ✔ Correct
  • [C] Keep your eyes to the right-hand side of the road
  • [D] Keep your eyes focused on the centre of the road

Of the four hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action if you are the driver of the blue car?
  • [A] The parked car
  • [B] The reversing car ✔ Correct
  • [C] The car coming towards you
  • [D] The car parked on the opposite side of the road
Explanation: The main hazard in this scenario is the reversing car. You should be prepared to stop as you may be in the car's blind spot.
Q0540 Class 1 (Car) Car - Emergencies Official NZTA & DT Driver Training Multiple Answers
The bonnet of your vehicle lifts up while you are driving and you cannot see. What should you do? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Brake suddenly so you don't leave the road
  • [B] Look through the gap underneath the bonnet or out of the side window ✔ Correct
  • [C] Signal, brake smoothly, and pull to the side of the road, then refasten the bonnet ✔ Correct
  • [D] Turn on your headlights and look out of the side window
Explanation: What happens if your bonnet latch fails? It's extremely unlikely that your bonnet latch or catch will fail. Almost all bonnet catches have a two-stage release so that if the first stage fails it catches on the second stage. However, it's not unheard of as you can see in this...
Q0541 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA & DT Driver Training
What is the FIRST action you should take if you are a driver involved in a crash?
  • [A] Contact the police
  • [B] Look and see if there are any injuries ✔ Correct
  • [C] Call the ambulance
  • [D] Run away from the scene to go and tell someone
  • [E] Contact a family member or friend
Explanation: First actions after a car crash If you are involved in a crash and not badly hurt, the first thing to do is check for other people's injuries. Then see if your vehicle can be moved out of danger once you have checked on other vehicle occupants and called emergency services....
Q0542 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
What is the safest thing to do when you are driving on a country road at night and your vehicle headlights suddenly go out? Select all that apply.
  • [A] Slow down and prepare to stop somewhere safe ✔ Correct
  • [B] Stop on the right so you are facing cars going by
  • [C] Turn your hazard lights on ✔ Correct
  • [D] Continue driving slowly with your hazard lights on
  • [E] Continue driving with your interior lights on
Explanation: If your lights are out, you won't be able to see where you are going and you won't be visible to other drivers. You should never park on the right facing traffic.
Q0543 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What should you do if you are driving past a line of parked cars and you notice a ball bouncing out into the road ahead?
  • [A] It doesn't matter if it hits the car, just keep driving on your side of the road
  • [B] Keep on your side of the road and stop safely ✔ Correct
  • [C] Try to avoid the ball by immediately swerving to the side of the road
  • [D] Flash your headlights
Explanation: Swerving to the other side of the road can create a hazard while hitting the ball might send it into the path of another vehicle.
Q0544 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What would happen if you were to have a front tyre blowout?
  • [A] The back end will sway to the right side of the blowout
  • [B] The back end will sway to either side of the blowout
  • [C] The front end will pull towards the side of the blowout ✔ Correct
  • [D] The front end will pull to the opposite side of the blowout
Explanation: When the wheel has a blowout, it is a smaller radius so this makes the car pull in the direction of the blowout and it becomes much more difficult for the wheel to rotate.
Q0545 All Classes Behaviour Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
When reversing your vehicle, how should you look for hazards? Check all that apply.
  • [A] Check your rear-view and wing mirrors before reversing ✔ Correct
  • [B] Look over your shoulder ✔ Correct
  • [C] Get out and walk around the vehicle ✔ Correct
  • [D] If you have any reversing sensors or cameras make sure they are turned on ✔ Correct
Explanation: These are all acceptable ways to check for hazards before reversing.
Q0546 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When should you pull over to let an ambulance or fire engine pass you?
  • [A] If it is travelling faster than you would like to
  • [B] You can speed up, you don't need to let it past you
  • [C] Only if it's red flashing lights and/or siren is flashing ✔ Correct
  • [D] You must allow it to pass you at all times
Explanation: You will need to pull over safely if you see a fire engine or ambulance with its red flashing lights and/or siren on and let it pass.
Q0547 All Classes Emergencies Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you see two red lights flashing outside of a fire station, what do you do?
  • [A] Prepare to stop by slowing down in case a vehicle leaves the fire station
  • [B] Remain stopped until the lights are no longer flashing ✔ Correct
  • [C] Slow down to 25kph and then proceed if it is safe to do so
Explanation: You must stop until they have stopped flashing, as red lights may operate outside of airports and fire stations.

  • [B] Six metres ✔ Correct
  • [C] 5 metres
  • [D] Two metres

  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No

Q0555 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi Multiple Answers
Does a broken yellow line painted close to the edge of the road indicate that you may stop or park your vehicle there at any time?
  • [A] Correct. ✔ Correct
  • [B] Incorrect ✔ Correct
Explanation: If there is a broken yellow line, you can't park there.
Q0556 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
This sign indicates what?
  • [A] Motorcycles and other private vehicles are allowed to park to the left of the sign
  • [B] Motorcycles are the only vehicle that are allowed to park left of the sign ✔ Correct
  • [C] Motorcycles are only allowed to park left of the sign
Explanation: To the left of the sign, motorcycles can park here. No other vehicle can park here.
Q0557 All Classes Parking Official NZTA & DT Driver Training Multiple Answers

  • [B] Turn your wheels away from the kerb
  • [C] Put your car in park if it has an automatic transmission or in reverse gear if it has manual transmission ✔ Correct
  • [D] Turn you low beams on
  • [E] Put your handbrake on ✔ Correct

Q0558 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign indicate?
  • [A] After you pass the sign you can stop ✔ Correct
  • [B] You cannot stop after this sign, only before
  • [C] Within 20 metres of this sign you can park
  • [D] You can't stop at all until parking permission is provided
Explanation: The end of a no-stopping zone or clearway is indicated by this sign.
Q0559 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] In the next 4km you can stop anywhere
  • [B] In the next 4km you must not stop anywhere ✔ Correct
Explanation: The distance shown under the sign is the distance you must stop.
Q0560 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] You are only allowed to stop to drop people off between 8 and 9am
  • [B] Between 7 and 9am you can park here
  • [C] You are not permitted to park here between 7 and 9am ✔ Correct
Explanation: This sign means that you must not stop here between the times indicated. If you stop, your car may be towed and you will have to pay a towing fee to get your car back.
Q0561 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
What does this sign mean?
  • [A] As long as you are stopped for 5 minutes or less then you are fine to stop here
  • [B] As long as a person remains with the car to move it you can stop here
  • [C] If you have children in the car then you can stop here.
  • [D] You can stop here only if you have a mobility parking permit ✔ Correct
Explanation: You must display a mobility parking permit on your front window in order to park here. If you fail to do so you may be fined or you may have your vehicle towed.
Q0562 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When are you permitted to park your car on the right hand side of the road?
  • [A] Only on a one-way street ✔ Correct
  • [B] If there are marked bays
  • [C] If you leave your park lights on then you can park on the right anytime
  • [D] If you are dropping passengers off
  • [E] in the city if there is no traffic coming
Explanation: If the marked bays are perpendicular to the road then answer b is correct. To ensure that you are not facing traffic, you must never park on the right.
Q0563 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When can you park your vehicle on a loading zone?
  • [A] Never - they're only for commercial vehicles
  • [B] Only weekends and after business hours you can park a car there
  • [C] You are only able to park there for the amount of time that is shown on the sign as long as you are unloading ✔ Correct
  • [D] It's between midnight and 5am
  • [E] At all times during business hours (8am to 6am)
Explanation: It's okay for a vehicle to stop here to unload, but it must not be left unattended for more than five minutes. If the vehicle is attended and is being unloaded it can remain in the car park for more than 5 minutes. If the sign said '5MIN MAXIMUM' then the vehicle would have to...
Q0564 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
When you are driving a private vehicle can you stop on a bus stop?
  • [A] Yes, if that vehicle has seven or more seats
  • [B] Only if it's outside of normal bus working hours
  • [C] No. Only buses are permitted to stop here. ✔ Correct
  • [D] Yes, if it's not a commercially licensed vehicle
  • [E] Yes, when picking up passengers
Explanation: Buses are the only vehicles permitted to stop at a bus stop. You may be fined otherwise.

  • [A] Yes ✔ Correct
  • [B] No

Q0566 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You can park your vehicle over a fire hydrant, when?
  • [A] It is never permitted
  • [B] Anytime you wish
  • [C] If there is someone who can stay with the vehicle that is able to move it in case of an emergency. ✔ Correct
Explanation: You are permitted to park your vehicle on or within 50cm of a fire hydrant (if someone who can move the vehicle stays with it).
Q0567 All Classes Parking Official NZTA / Waka Kotahi
You may park your vehicle on a loading zone when?
  • [A] They're only for commercial vehicles
  • [B] On weekends and after business hours you can park here
  • [C] For the purposes of unloading you can park at any time, but only for the amount of time shown on the sign ✔ Correct
  • [D] Only between 6am and midnight
  • [E] At all times during business hours (8am to 6am)
Explanation: For the purposes of unloading you can park any vehicle in a loading zone. However, you must not park a private vehicle there if there is an additional sign underneath that specifically only permits goods vehicles.

  • [A] Left ✔ Correct
